chunk_findings.detail: The default glob is `ddflow/**`, and the accompanying doc claims "Tests, docs and `.ddflow/**` are not listed and so are exempt." That claim is false for the default: a git pathspec `ddflow/**` matches every path recursively under `ddflow/`, including `ddflow/tests/**.py` and any test directories/files inside the package. Concrete scenario: a task commits only `ddflow/tests/test_config.py` (a test-only change). The landed diff changes a path matching `readme_code_globs`, README.md is untouched, and no `docs` skip is recorded, so the per-task check fires — contradicting the stated acceptance criterion "Never block a test-only ... change" and the intent's "Test-only and docs-only changes ... never match." The only way to honor the documented exemption with this config is for the (not-shown) implementation to carry additional test-file detection logic independent of the globs; if it relies on "tests are not listed" as the doc asserts, test-only changes under `ddflow/` produce spurious reports. Either the default glob must exclude test paths or the doc sentence must not claim the globs themselves provide the exemption.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config.py:972 (`readme_code_globs` default `["ddflow/**"]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The docs line is appended only when `repo is not None and not suggested`. `suggested` is the view's precomputed list of suggested next actions (the same view already derives `todo`/`gates remaining` from the pipeline). When that list is non-empty — the normal state for a task that still has gates left, i.e. exactly the state the per-task docs check is meant to surface — the whole `readme_report` branch is skipped, so `ddflow brief` prints no `- docs: README not updated` line. For a task that changed `ddflow/**` and not `README.md` while a gate is still pending, `brief` shows `- gates remaining: ... → ...` plus the suggested commands but omits the docs warning, directly contradicting the added driver text ("`complete`, `ddflow gate status` and `ddflow brief` all say `README not updated`") and the acceptance criterion that the task "is reported". Gating the report on `not suggested` makes the brief output depend on an unrelated field rather than on the docs condition itself.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py:349

chunk_findings.detail: The stated acceptance for D-readme-current is: "*the driver doc and the per-agent deltas say so*." The only test that guards this deliverable (`test_the_driver_says_so`) checks just `docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md` and `ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md`, and its docstring explicitly declares "The per-agent deltas restate nothing by design (every harness reads the driver)." That is the author recording that the per-agent deltas were deliberately *not* updated with the `ddflow gate skip <id> docs` instruction, which is exactly the acceptance criterion that was dropped. There is no assertion anywhere in the change that a delta file contains the new instruction, so the requirement is both unmet and untested — the loop over `(driver, template)` should also cover the per-agent delta files (or the acceptance should not claim they say so).

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_test_path` only recognizes directories literally named `test`/`tests`, filenames starting with `test_`, filenames ending in `_test.py`, `conftest.py`, or `.test.js`/`.test.ts`/`.spec.js`/`.spec.ts`. Standard test layouts escape this heuristic. Concretely, a task that changes only `ddflow/webapp/__tests__/helper.ts` or `ddflow/webapp/Foo.test.tsx` (or `ddflow/webapp/Foo.spec.tsx`, or `spec/models/foo_spec.rb`): none of these match, so the path flows into `code = [p for p in changed if is_shared(...) and not _is_test_path(p)]`, `code` is non-empty, and in `[enforce].readme_with_code = "block"` mode the item is blocked with "README not updated". That directly violates the stated acceptance "Never block a test-only ... change." The omission is visible from the code itself: it explicitly handles `.test.js`/`.spec.js`/`.test.ts`/`.spec.ts` but not the `.tsx`/`.jsx` variants nor the dominant Jest `__tests__/` or RSpec `spec/` conventions, so the intent to cover JS/TS tests is only partially implemented. (The heuristic also cuts the other way: a real production change under a directory literally named `test`, e.g. `ddflow/services/test/handler.py`, is silently excluded and produces a false negative.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py `_is_test_path` (used by `readme_report`)

chunk_findings.detail: The task spec defines the watched code as "ddflow/** (or the configured paths)", and the only docs file exempted is one matching `enforce.readme_files` (default `README.md`, anchored at root by `_is_readme`). A docs-only task that touches markdown inside the code tree — e.g. changing only `ddflow/docs/design.md` — therefore lands in `code` (it matches `ddflow/**` and is not a test path), README.md is untouched, and in `block` mode the item is blocked. The acceptance says "Never block a test-only or docs-only change"; only test-only changes are actually special-cased, and docs-only is handled solely for the configured README filename, so any other documentation change under the configured code globs is treated as code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py `readme_report` (the `code = [...]` filter)

chunk_findings.detail: The check exempts test-only changes (`_is_test_path`) but has no exemption for docs-only changes, even though the intent states "Never block a test-only or docs-only change." Any documentation file that lives inside the configured code globs is treated as code. Concretely, with the default-shaped config (`[enforce].readme_with_code = "block"`, `readme_code_globs = ["ddflow/**"]`), a task whose only changes are e.g. `ddflow/AGENTS.md` (or `ddflow/docs/usage.md`, i.e. the "driver doc"/per-agent deltas this repo keeps) produces `changed = ["ddflow/AGENTS.md"]`; `is_shared("ddflow/AGENTS.md", ["ddflow/**"])` is true, `_is_test_path` is false (no `test`/`tests` component, name does not match the test-name suffixes), and no root `README.md` is in `changed`, so `readme_report` returns `README_REMEDY` and `blocks = (mode == "block") and readme != README_UNKNOWN` is true, appending the report to `v.blockers`. A pure documentation change is therefore blocked in `block` mode, contradicting the acceptance clause. `_is_test_path` covers the test half of that clause but there is no analogous `_is_doc_path`/`.md`-style exemption (or equivalent restriction of `readme_code_globs` to source extensions), so the docs half is unimplemented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:readme_report / `_is_test_path`

chunk_findings.detail: The new block passes `item` to `readme_report`, but the item in scope in this function is named `it`. The surrounding lines in the same function all use `it` for the item being rendered — `pipeline_for(it, cfg)`, `it.gate_outcome(g)`, and `it.body` a couple of lines below the hunk — and `item` appears nowhere else in the function or its visible signature. Running `ddflow brief` on any item (the guard `repo is not None and not suggested` is the normal path) therefore raises `NameError: name 'item' is not defined` before the docs line can be appended, so the very output the driver doc promises ("`complete`, `ddflow gate status` and `ddflow brief` all say `README not updated`") is never produced by `brief`; the command crashes instead. The fix is to pass `it` (or whatever the local item binding is actually called), matching the rest of the function.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py:349 (`readme_report(state, cfg, item, repo=repo)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance criteria require that "the driver doc **and the per-agent deltas** say so" — i.e. an agent that reads only its per-agent delta must learn to record `docs` skip/outcome. This test only asserts the literal string `"ddflow gate skip <id> docs"` is present in the two *driver* files (`docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md`, `ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md`); it does not touch, and nothing else in the changed test file touches, the per-agent deltas. Worse, the test's own docstring states "The per-agent deltas restate nothing by design (every harness reads the driver)," which is a deliberate decision *not* to satisfy that acceptance item: if the deltas are separate artifacts that agents actually read, then an agent driven by a delta (rather than the driver) is never told about the new `README not updated` / `gate skip <id> docs --reason` path, so the message that `complete`/`gate status` now emit is undiscoverable from the artifact that agent consumes. Given the acceptance wording, the change is incomplete: either the deltas must be updated to mention the skip, or the acceptance item should be renegotiated; a test that only checks the driver does not demonstrate the requirement holds.

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_test_or_doc_path` recognizes documentation only by file suffix (`.md`, `.rst`, `.adoc`, `.txt`) and never by directory, so a docs-only change to a non-text artifact that lives under a code glob is misclassified as code. Given the stated default code globs (`ddflow/**`), take a task whose entire landed diff is `ddflow/docs/architecture.svg` (or `ddflow/docs/schema.yaml`): `is_shared("ddflow/docs/architecture.svg", ["ddflow/**"])` is true and `_is_test_or_doc_path` returns false, so `code` is non-empty and `readme_report` returns `README_REMEDY` even though no user-visible code changed and the README logically need not move. Under `[enforce].readme_with_code = block` this blocks a docs-only change, directly contradicting the requirement "Never block a test-only or docs-only change" (and under the default `warn` it emits a spurious "README not updated" report for a docs asset). Adding `"doc"/"docs"` to the excluded directory set in that predicate, or treating paths under a docs directory as non-code, is what the acceptance implies.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py::_is_test_or_doc_path

chunk_findings.detail: The stated acceptance for this change is: "the driver doc **and the per-agent deltas** say so." The only test that checks the documentation requirement is `test_the_driver_says_so`, and it asserts the string only in the two driver docs (`docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md` and `ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md`). Its docstring states outright: *"The per-agent deltas restate nothing by design (every harness reads the driver)."* That is the author acknowledging the per-agent deltas were not updated and will not be updated, which is exactly the half of the acceptance that is left unimplemented. Concretely, an agent harness whose deltas/instruction files are the only thing it reads (the situation the acceptance clause exists to cover) will never see `ddflow gate skip <id> docs` and will keep landing `ddflow/**` changes without a README update or a recorded skip, so the gate is invisible to that path. Because the test deliberately asserts nothing about the deltas, this gap cannot be caught by the suite. The fix is either to add the sentence to the per-agent delta files and assert it, or to get the acceptance amended instead of silently narrowing it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_docs_per_task.py::test_the_driver_says_so

chunk_findings.detail:
`changed_paths` can return `[]` (an empty list) where its own docstring promises it returns `None` for "git cannot say what changed", and `readme_report` treats `[]` as "no code changed" rather than as "unknown", so the task silently escapes the check. Concretely, in the branch fallback:

```python
if it.branch and W.rev(repo, it.branch):
    out = W.git_paths(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", f"{base}...{it.branch}")
    return None if out is None else sorted(out)
```

Consider a `--no-worktree` task with no `landed_before`/`landed_after` recorded (so the landed branch is not taken) whose worktree is gone (so the `TS.changed_files` branch is not taken). If its branch has already been merged into `base`, or if `it.branch` is the same as `base` (which happens when `it.base` is unset and `base` falls back to `W.default_branch(repo)`, i.e. a driver committing directly on the default branch), then `git diff base...branch` is `diff(merge-base(base,branch), branch)` = `diff(branch, branch)`, which prints nothing. `sorted([])` is `[]`, so `readme_report` reaches `if not code or ...: return ""` and reports nothing at all — even though the item's landed change to `ddflow/**` left README.md untouched. The intended answer in that situation is `README_UNKNOWN` ("nobody looked is not no", per the same docstring), not silence, and the acceptance criterion "a task that changes ddflow/** without README.md is reported" is violated. The `[]` result is indistinguishable from a genuine no-op diff, so the caller cannot tell the two apart.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py `changed_paths` (branch fallback) / `readme_report`

chunk_findings.detail:
The brief renderer works with the item object under the name `it` — the surrounding lines are `pipeline_for(it, cfg)`, `it.gate_outcome(g)`, `it.body` — but the new docs check passes `item`:

```python
if repo is not None and not suggested:
    from ..services.completion import readme_report
    readme = readme_report(state, cfg, item, repo=repo)
```

`item` is not the name the function binds for the item (the function uses `it` throughout, e.g. `if it.body:` two lines later), so this either raises `NameError: name 'item' is not defined` or, if a local `item` exists holding the raw id/dict rather than the item object, hands `readme_report` the wrong object (it expects the item, since it is given `state`, `cfg` and the item to compute gate outcomes/paths). The failure is masked in the common test path because the branch is guarded by `repo is not None`: any render with `repo=None` never executes it, while `ddflow brief` run inside a repo takes the branch and blows up (or prints a bogus/none docs result). It should pass `it`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py (the new `readme_report` call)

chunk_findings.detail: The helper that is supposed to keep "test-only" changes from being reported only recognizes a narrow set of Python/JS-ish conventions. A change that touches nothing but test code still lands in `code` (because `is_shared(p, cfg.enforce.readme_code_globs)` is true and `_is_test_or_doc_path(p)` returns False), so `not code` is False and `readme_report` returns the "README not updated" report — which, in `block` mode, blocks a task that changed no user-visible code, contradicting the stated requirement "Never block a test-only … change." Concrete inputs: `ddflow/src/main/java/com/x/FooTest.java` (Java's standard `*Test` convention: `parts[:-1]` contains no member of `_TEST_DOC_DIRS`, `name.startswith("test_")` is False, `stem = "FooTest"` does not end with `_test`/`_spec`, and `".test."`/`".spec."` are absent), `ddflow/widgetSpec.js` (camelCase spec), `ddflow/integration_tests/helpers.py` (`integration_tests` is not in `_TEST_DOC_DIRS`), or `ddflow/Tests/foo.py` (`_TEST_DOC_DIRS` comparison is case-sensitive). For each, with code globs `ddflow/**` and no README touched, `code` is non-empty and the report is emitted, so the check fires on a test-only diff.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:_is_test_or_doc_path

chunk_findings.detail:
The suppression test is written as
`docs and docs.outcome in ("passed", "skipped") and (docs.reason or docs.evidence)`,
so *either* field silences the check for *either* outcome. But the change's own contract (the `README_REMEDY` text: "record the section you changed, or `ddflow gate skip <id> docs --reason ...`", and the docstring which maps `gate skip ... --reason` to `skipped` and `gate record ... --outcome passed --evidence <section>` to `passed`) requires the fields to be outcome-specific: a skip must carry a *reason*, and a passed outcome must carry *evidence* (the README section that moved). Input that demonstrates the hole: an item whose `docs` gate has `outcome == "passed"` with `reason` set and `evidence == ""` (e.g. recorded as `gate record <id> docs --outcome passed --reason "n/a"` without `--evidence`). The condition evaluates `docs.reason` truthy and `readme_report` returns `""`, i.e. it treats the code-only change as documented even though no changed section was recorded at all — exactly the case the acceptance says must be reported. Symmetrically, a `docs` gate with `outcome == "skipped"` and `evidence` set but no `reason` also returns `""`, although the requirement is that a skip needs a reason. The check should be outcome-keyed, e.g. `(docs.outcome == "passed" and docs.evidence) or (docs.outcome == "skipped" and docs.reason)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:readme_report (the `docs` guard)
